title: Best Men's Puffer and Down Jackets UK
short: Down and puffer jackets compared by fill power, weight and warmth, from everyday high street to technical mountain kit.
intro: Down jackets range from thin everyday puffers to technical mountain layers rated for sub-zero conditions. This guide compares jackets tested by Live for the Outdoors (Trail magazine) in winter mountain conditions, alongside a high-street budget option, so you can match the warmth and price to how you'll actually wear it.

guide.a: Fill power measures how much a given weight of down expands to fill space, roughly reflecting insulation quality. Higher numbers (800-1,000) mean warmer, more compressible down for the same weight, and typically cost more.

guide.q: How warm a jacket do I actually need for UK weather?
guide.a: For most UK winters, a jacket with 600-800 fill power and moderate down weight is usually enough for everyday wear and hiking. Save the heaviest, most technical jackets here for genuinely cold mountain conditions or exposed winter hillwalking.

Down offers the best warmth-to-weight ratio and packs smaller, but loses much of its insulating power when wet unless treated with a hydrophobic coating. Synthetic insulation is heavier for the same warmth but keeps insulating even when damp, which suits persistently wet UK conditions.

guide.q: Do I need a hooded jacket?
guide.a: A hood adds warmth and weather protection for hillwalking or exposed conditions. For everyday city wear, a hood is a matter of preference rather than necessity, and some jackets, like the Haglofs base model here, skip it to save weight and cost.
